title: Parcel Checkpoints
statement: A depot stores the signed change in parcel count at each checkpoint in parcels. For every pair [start, end] in ranges, return the total change from index start up to but not including index end. Return the totals in the same order as ranges. A range with start equal to end is empty and has total zero.
constraints: Each range satisfies 0 <= start <= end <= parcels.length.

examples.explanation: The requested slices are [4,-2], [-2,7,3], and an empty slice.
The only valid slice of an empty array is empty.

hints.content: Solving one range by summing its entries is straightforward; many overlapping ranges repeat work.
Can one stored cumulative total help answer several different ranges?
Let prefix[k] mean the sum of the first k entries.
A range total is prefix[end] minus prefix[start].
Begin the prefix array with zero, accumulate every checkpoint once, and answer each range with one subtraction.

testCases.explanation: The requested slices are [4,-2], [-2,7,3], and an empty slice.
The only valid slice of an empty array is empty.
Signed totals may be zero or negative.
No requested ranges means no output entries.
Each answer uses the requested half-open range.

solutions.title: Walk each requested range
solutions.intuition: Every answer can be obtained directly from the checkpoint changes included in that range.
solutions.approach: For each range, add the entries from start through end - 1 and append the result.
solutions.pseudocode: For each [start, end): set total = 0; add each included parcel change; append total.
solutions.timeComplexity: O(n × q) in the worst case, for n checkpoints and q ranges
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(q) for the returned answers; O(1) additional working space
commonMistakes: Treating end as inclusive introduces an off-by-one error.
Forgetting the leading zero makes ranges beginning at index zero harder to handle correctly.
solutions.interviewExplanation: With many overlapping queries, repeated summation wastes work. I preprocess the checkpoint changes into prefix totals and answer each query in constant time. The end-exclusive convention also makes empty ranges work without a special branch.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Every answer can be obtained directly from the checkpoint changes included in that range.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: For each range, add the entries from start through end - 1 and append the result.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: After exploring every allowed candidate, return the best valid result under the statement’s rules.

solutions.title: Reuse cumulative totals
solutions.intuition: The difference of two prefix totals removes exactly the entries before the requested start.
solutions.approach: Create a prefix array of length n + 1 with prefix[0] = 0. Return prefix[end] - prefix[start] for each range.
solutions.pseudocode: Build prefix starting at zero; for each range return prefix[end] - prefix[start].
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(n + q), including the returned answers
commonMistakes: Treating end as inclusive introduces an off-by-one error.
Forgetting the leading zero makes ranges beginning at index zero harder to handle correctly.
solutions.interviewExplanation: With many overlapping queries, repeated summation wastes work. I preprocess the checkpoint changes into prefix totals and answer each query in constant time. The end-exclusive convention also makes empty ranges work without a special branch.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Range [0,2) totals prefix[2] - prefix[0] = 2; range [1,4) totals 12 - 4 = 8.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: Range [2,2) subtracts the same prefix total from itself and returns zero.
